chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): May Allah improve you. For the time of each prayer, is the beginning of the time best, or its middle, or its end? He said: 'The beginning.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Allah loves from the good that which is hastened.'

key_terms.أَوَّلُ الْوَقْتِ: The beginning of the prayer time

ai.seo_question: Which part of the prayer time is considered best for performing salat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that the beginning of the prayer time is superior, citing the Prophetic tradition that 'Allah loves for the good to be hastened.' This establishes the principle of *al-‘ajal* (promptness) in worship, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence distinguishing between the preferred time (*al-awwal al-waqt*) and the time of necessity (*waqt al-hajah*). The chain of transmission through Zurarah and Ibn Abi Umayr highlights the reliability of this ruling within the Imami scholarly tradition.
